name: Sweden
dek: Stockholm Observatoriekullen, WMO 02485. Not the north.
paragraphs: The reference station is Stockholm Observatoriekullen, WMO 02485, height 43 m, the observatory hill in the capital. An automatic station at the same coordinates (WMO 02484) has temperatures but no precipitation column and was not used. The north of Sweden is not this table.

The highest average high in the table is 23.6 °C, in July. The lowest average low is -3.2 °C, in February. The wettest month by the precipitation column is August, at 66.2 mm, and the driest is March, at 27.3 mm.

climate.caption: Reference station: Stockholm Observatoriekullen, WMO 02485. An automatic station at the same coordinates, WMO 02484, has temperatures but no precipitation column and was not used.
climate.note: World Meteorological Organization 1991–2020 climatological standard normals, distributed by NOAA NCEI. Monthly values are copied as printed, with leading spaces removed; a value printed with no leading zero, such as -.3, is shown as -0.3.

plugs.label: Plugs and voltage
plugs.value: Type C and F, 230 V, 50 Hz
plugs.detail: The IEC world-plugs list, in the copy archived on 16 August 2026, shows Sweden at the voltage, frequency, and plug types in the figure. A direct download of the live page did not return the list, so the archive is the copy that was read.

driving.label: Driving side
driving.detail: Visit Sweden, Sweden's official tourism site, says: "Drive on the right: Like most European countries, Swedes drive on the right side of the road." The same page says headlights must be on at all times, including in daylight.

tipping.label: Tipping
tipping.value: Welcome but not expected; rounding up is common
tipping.detail: Visit Sweden, Sweden's official tourism site, says tipping in Sweden "isn't as established as in many other countries. It's always welcome but not expected." It says that when eating out it is common to round up to the nearest big number, and gives the example of a 280 SEK bill rounded to 300 SEK. It adds that a service charge is sometimes included and will be clearly stated on the bill.

water.label: Tap water
water.detail: CDC's traveler page for Sweden, last reviewed August 25, 2026, does not say whether tap water is safe or unsafe. It says food and water standards around the world vary based on the destination, that standards may also differ within a country, and that risk may change depending on the activity. It points readers to CDC's food and water precautions. This page does not turn that into medical advice.

currency.label: Currency
currency.detail: ISO 4217 lists the currency name Swedish Krona and the code SEK for Sweden.

timeZone.label: Time zone
timeZone.detail: IANA's zone.tab gives Sweden one row, Europe/Stockholm. zone1970.tab lists that zone on a row named Europe/Berlin, which it shares with Germany, Denmark, Norway, and Svalbard and Jan Mayen. The backward file links Europe/Stockholm to Europe/Berlin. The sheet prints the zone.tab name.

entry.label: Official entry requirements
entry.note: The Migration Agency's page on visiting Sweden. We do not restate a visa rule.
